draft.title: Using dashes
card: A dash is a long line in writing. It is longer than a hyphen, which joins words.
Extra idea
A single dash can add an extra idea to the end of a sentence that is already complete.
Pause
A single dash can also make a dramatic pause before a surprise or a twist.
Pair
A pair of dashes around an aside works like brackets, but it draws more attention to the aside.
draft.remember: Dashes add an idea, a pause or an aside, and they make readers notice it.

a.q: Why might a writer put an aside between a pair of dashes instead of brackets?
opts: To draw more attention to the aside
To make the aside less noticeable
To join two main clauses without a conjunction
To turn a verb into a noun
a.why: A pair of dashes works like brackets, but it makes the aside stand out more. Brackets tend to tuck the aside away, so the second option has the effect reversed.
a.clue: Think about which punctuation makes readers notice the aside.

b.q: Jin writes a sentence about a race. He adds a single dash before the surprising last part. What effect does the dash have?
opts: It makes a dramatic pause before the surprise
It makes a quiet aside that is easy to miss
It ends the sentence early like a full stop
It turns a verb into a noun
b.why: A single dash can set up a dramatic pause before a twist. A quiet aside is the effect of brackets, not of a dash placed before a surprise.
b.clue: Picture the reader waiting a moment before the twist.

a.best: To draw more attention to the aside

b.best: It makes a dramatic pause before the surprise

proposal.title: Using dashes
card: A dash is a long line in writing. It is longer than a hyphen, which joins two words into one, as in well-known.
Extra idea
A single dash can add an extra idea to the end of a sentence that is already complete. For example, a writer finishes a sentence about a storm, then adds a dash and the words and the power went out.
Pause
A single dash can also make a dramatic pause before a surprise or a twist. The reader stops for a moment, which builds suspense.
Pair
A pair of dashes around an aside works like brackets, but it draws more attention to the aside. Brackets tend to tuck the aside away.
proposal.remember: One dash adds an idea or a pause. Two dashes mark an aside more strongly than brackets.

a.q: Why might a writer put an aside between a pair of dashes instead of brackets?
opts: To draw more attention to the aside
To make the aside less noticeable
To show the aside is a direct quote
To join the aside to the next word
a.why: A pair of dashes works like brackets, but it makes the aside stand out more. The option about making the aside less noticeable has it reversed: that is what brackets tend to do.
a.clue: Which one, dashes or brackets, tucks an aside away?

b.q: Jin describes a long race. He adds a single dash, then reveals that the winner was his little sister. What effect does the dash have?
opts: It makes readers stop briefly before the reveal
It tucks the reveal away so readers may skip it
It joins the reveal to the race as one word
It marks the reveal as something Jin quoted
b.why: A single dash can make a dramatic pause, so readers wait a moment before the twist. Tucking words away so they are easy to miss is what brackets tend to do, not a dash.
b.clue: Think about what a reader does when they reach the dash.

a.best: To draw more attention to the aside

b.best: It makes readers stop briefly before the reveal
